description: Single source of truth for threat-modeling-prefill. Holds (a) the risk-scoring rules (the real SFS occurrence x impact matrix and the real countermeasure-efficiency formula), (b) the STRIDE-LM category reference, and (c) the selection logic that maps an application's architecture signals to a subset of the bundled real scenario catalog. Read by assets/scripts/build-threatmodel.ps1 AND cited by any generated doc/README. Never duplicate this table into a .md or hard-code it in a script. All generated scenarios are CANDIDATES to validate with the security team - never acquired.

catalogSource.note: v1.0 of this skill shipped only 4 generic, hand-written prefillRules - far thinner than the real SFS catalog and the real cause of a reported defect ('Le threat modeling ne va pas du tout'). v2.0 bundles the ACTUAL SFS STRIDE-LM scenario catalog and countermeasure library, supplied by the user from the live Cybersecurity TM tool, instead of a few invented heuristics.
catalogSource.threatCatalog: references/threat-catalog.json - 176 real scenarios (id TM1..TM176), extracted verbatim from TM_Threat_portfolio.csv. Each has: category, scope[], element, threat, atRest/inTransit/inUse, stride[] (S/T/R/I/D/E/LM), description, examples, realExampleLink, counterMeasureIds[], counterMeasureTitles[], priority. 47 of them (category=Applicative) also carry sampleOccurrence/sampleImpact/sampleRiskLevel taken from a real, security-team-rated project workbook - these are an ILLUSTRATIVE starting point only, never a default to apply silently; every project rates its own occurrence/impact with the project + security team.
catalogSource.countermeasureLibrary: references/countermeasure-library.json - 97 real countermeasures (CM.xxx), extracted verbatim from the 'Controls and CM' sheet of Applicative_Model_with_new_Risk_module_threat_modelling.xlsx. Each has: type (Preventive/Detective/Corrective/Recovery/Deterrent), category (Technical/Administrative/Physical), description, occurrenceMitigation (1-3), impactMitigation (1-3), easeOfImplementation (1-3).
catalogSource.strideLibrary: references/stride-library.json - the official STRIDE-LM definitions, defence objective, explanation, a cloud example and a mitigation-concept note per code, extracted verbatim from the 'Library' sheet of the same workbook.

engine.note: The module embeds no intelligence of its own. For a scenario taken from references/threat-catalog.json, its wording is the catalog's own real text - never re-generated or paraphrased by a model call. A model call (Bedrock by default; SFS Assist only as an optional conversational layer if a dialog need is confirmed) is used ONLY to word a genuinely CUSTOM scenario that the project team raises and that has no match in the catalog (mark it 'custom': true - see model-schema.md).

scales.note: This is the REAL SFS scale (occurrence 1-3 x impact 1-3), not the previously invented 1-4/1-16 scale. Do not relabel 1/2/3 beyond what the source workbook defines: it names only the resulting riskLevel band, not each individual occurrence/impact level - leave occurrence/impact as bare integers 1-3 and let riskLevel carry the label.

riskLevel.source: Threat_modeling sheet, column S formula, of the real SFS TM workbook - reproduced exactly, do not alter.
riskLevel.formula: riskLevel = matrix[occurrence][impact], occurrence and impact each in {1,2,3}

bandWeights.note: Used only to compute countermeasure efficiency below (MAX across the threats a countermeasure addresses) - not a second risk scale.

countermeasureEfficiency.source: Controls and CM sheet, column H formula, of the real SFS TM workbook - reproduced exactly, do not alter.
countermeasureEfficiency.formula: efficiency = occurrenceMitigation x impactMitigation x easeOfImplementation x bandWeight(threatLevel)
countermeasureEfficiency.threatLevel: threatLevel = the HIGHEST riskLevel band (by bandWeight) among every scenario this countermeasure is linked to via counterMeasureIds in threat-catalog.json (or countermeasures explicitly listed for a custom scenario). Recompute threatLevel/efficiency per project from the project's own occurrence/impact ratings - never reuse another project's efficiency number.
countermeasureEfficiency.note: This REPLACES the previously invented 0-3 'countermeasure effectiveness' scale, which had no basis in the real tool. A countermeasure is not rated in isolation; its value depends on which rated threats it mitigates.

scenarioSelection.note: REPLACES the 4 generic v1.0 prefillRules. Select candidate scenarios from references/threat-catalog.json by matching the application's real architecture signals against category/scope/element - do not hand-pick a handful of 'representative' scenarios and do not silently drop a category that applies.
steps: 1. From the DAT + dataflow + questionnaire, determine which catalog categories apply: 'Applicative' (almost always, any application has a Data-flow/Data store/Process/External entity/Trust boundary), 'CI/CD' (if the project has its own pipeline/supply chain, not only the shared SFS chain), 'Infra cloud' (AWS Landing Zone / account-level signals), 'EKS' (if Kubernetes/EKS is used), 'SaaS' (if a third-party SaaS is integrated), 'LLM IA' (if the application calls or embeds an LLM / GenAI component).

2. Within each applicable category, keep every catalog entry whose scope[] intersects the application's real scope (Application / Infrastructure / Network / External / Management / Physical / Supply Chain) - do not filter by element unless the project team confirms an element type genuinely does not exist in this architecture (e.g. no 'Data store' because the app is stateless).

3. For a signal that genuinely has no match in the catalog, raise it as a CUSTOM scenario: word it via the model call (engine.default), mark 'custom': true, and still score it with the real occurrence/impact/riskLevel scale above - never skip scoring a custom scenario.

4. Never silently narrow the catalog to a 'representative sample' to keep the deliverable short - a real past delivery did exactly that (7 hand-picked scenarios instead of covering the real catalog) and was rejected. If the full applicable subset is large, that is expected; list it in full and let the project + security team triage priority, rather than Claude/Kiro pre-triaging by omission.

5. For every kept scenario, carry its real counterMeasureIds/counterMeasureTitles from the catalog as the starting countermeasures column; look up each CM.xxx's occurrenceMitigation/impactMitigation/easeOfImplementation in references/countermeasure-library.json to compute efficiency once occurrence/impact are rated (step below).

nistReference.note: This mapping is an SFS/ARB-reporting addition layered on top of the real catalog (the source TM tool does not include a NIST mapping) - treat it as a starting point for the security team, never as part of the catalog's own authority, and never let it replace or relabel a catalog scenario's real STRIDE-LM flags.
